<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915834_theRebbe_708" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915834_theRebbe_708__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the sin of "abandoning My Torah" refers to not reciting a blessing over the Torah beforehand, which is the essential act of drawing down Ein Sof into the Torah itself.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood with a preface from the saying of our Rabbis, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="2">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="3">"For what has the land been destroyed?... Because they abandoned My Torah, because they did not bless the Torah first,"</t>
    <t s="4">From this it is understood</t>
    <t s="5">that the matter of "bless the Torah first" is a fundamental matter not only in the service of man in general</t>
    <t s="6">(to the extent that because they did not bless the Torah, the land was destroyed)</t>
    <t s="7">but also in the study of Torah itself,</t>
    <t s="8">for</t>
    <t s="9">("they did not bless the Torah first")</t>
    <t s="10">is called in the verse "they abandoned My Torah"</t>
    <t s="11">(the abandonment of Torah).</t>
    <t s="12">However, this is not an abandonment of Torah in general,</t>
    <t s="13">but rather,</t>
    <t s="14">as the verse states, "they abandoned My Torah"</t>
    <t s="15">(the Torah of the Holy One, blessed be He).</t>
    <t s="16">For the matter of "bless the Torah first" is to draw down,</t>
    <t s="17">the drawing down of blessing and abundance into the Torah,</t>
    <t s="18">and as is also understood from the language "bless the Torah"</t>
    <t s="19">(for ostensibly it should have said "bless before",</t>
    <t s="20">before the study of Torah,</t>
    <t s="21">and what is "bless the Torah"?),</t>
    <t s="22">for "blessing" is a term of drawing down, like one who "bends" (mavrich)</t>
    <t s="23">the vine</t>
    <t s="24">[And this matter</t>
    <t s="25">(sowing and planting,</t>
    <t s="26">including the bending of the vine)</t>
    <t s="27">is particularly relevant here,</t>
    <t s="28">for Torah and its mitzvos are a matter of sowing in the land],</t>
    <t s="29">and "bless the Torah" is the matter of drawing down Ein Sof into the Torah.</t>
    <t s="30">And it is the matter of engaging in Torah for its own sake, for the sake of the Torah itself,</t>
    <t s="31">to draw into it the revelation of Ein Sof that is above wisdom,</t>
    <t s="32">and in the manner of what is said in the Book of Bahir</t>
    <t s="33">and in the Book Maayan HaChochmah,</t>
    <t s="34">that Dovid would compose Torah with the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="35">And this is "because they abandoned My Torah, because they did not bless the Torah first,"</t>
    <t s="36">for by means of blessing the Torah, it becomes "My Torah"</t>
    <t s="37">[that one draws Ein Sof into it],</t>
    <t s="38">and when they did not bless the Torah first, it is "they abandoned My Torah,"</t>
    <t s="39">for the Torah then is as it is in its own essence and the revelation of Ein Sof is not drawn into it</t>
    <t s="40">(which is above wisdom).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section clarifies that even Torah studied by an impure person is still God's Torah, but the revelation of Ein Sof within it remains hidden, unlike the revealed level achieved through blessing the Torah first.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And even though the Torah as it is in its own essence is also the Torah of the Holy One, blessed be He, for He and His wisdom are one,</t>
    <t s="1">and even when an impure person studies it, it is the words of the Holy One, blessed be He, and therefore</t>
    <t s="2">it does not receive impurity, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="3">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="4">"Behold, My words are like fire," just as fire does not receive impurity, so too the words of Torah do not receive impurity,</t>
    <t s="5">[for even though an impure person who studies the Torah is not connected to the service of composing Torah with the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="6">and is also not connected to the service of "bless the Torah first" to draw down Ein Sof into the Torah,</t>
    <t s="7">nevertheless, even his Torah is the words of the Holy One, blessed be He, and is compared to fire, whose nature is to ascend</t>
    <t s="8">upward],</t>
    <t s="9">it is nevertheless understood</t>
    <t s="10">that this—that the Torah studied by an impure person is the words and wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He, for He and His wisdom are one—</t>
    <t s="11">is in a state of concealment,</t>
    <t s="12">and it is not comparable to the level of Torah that is "My Torah"</t>
    <t s="13">(the Torah of the Holy One, blessed be He)</t>
    <t s="14">in a revealed manner.</t>
    <t s="15">And particularly since the matter of "bless the Torah first" is</t>
    <t s="16">(as above)</t>
    <t s="17">to draw down into the Torah the revelation of Ein Sof that is above wisdom.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the superiority of Torah study after prayer is that it is done with self-nullification, enabling the drawing down of Ein Sof into the Torah, connecting the two interpretations of the ladder in the Midrash as prayer and Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this it will be understood</t>
    <t s="2">that the superiority in the study of Torah after prayer is not only regarding the study</t>
    <t s="3">(of the person),</t>
    <t s="4">that his study after the preparation of the service of prayer is in the manner of "those who love Your Torah"</t>
    <t s="5">(as above in section 2),</t>
    <t s="6">but also regarding the Torah</t>
    <t s="7">(that he studies),</t>
    <t s="8">for the matter of "bless the Torah first,"</t>
    <t s="9">the drawing down of Ein Sof into the Torah,</t>
    <t s="10">is</t>
    <t s="11">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="12">in the study of Torah after the preparation of the service of prayer.</t>
    <t s="13">And the explanation:</t>
    <t s="14">for in order to draw down Ein Sof into the Torah, it is</t>
    <t s="15">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="16">when the study of Torah is with self-nullification (bittul).</t>
    <t s="17">And in order for the study of Torah to be with self-nullification, this is achieved through the preparation of the service of prayer.</t>
    <t s="18">For prayer is a matter of self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="19">for during prayer one must stand as a servant before his master,</t>
    <t s="20">which is a self-nullification superior even to the self-nullification of the Shema.</t>
    <t s="21">For in the Shema, although it is forbidden to hint with one's eyes, or to motion with one's lips, or to point with one's fingers,</t>
    <t s="22">nevertheless there are several matters for which one may interrupt the Shema,</t>
    <t s="23">unlike in prayer.</t>
    <t s="24">And even the Shema is</t>
    <t s="25">(also)</t>
    <t s="26">said while sitting, unlike prayer which is</t>
    <t s="27">(specifically)</t>
    <t s="28">while standing, to the extent that there is no standing except for prayer,</t>
    <t s="29">for the difference between sitting and standing is that sitting indicates a matter of settlement</t>
    <t s="30">[This is what Rashi explains on the verse,</t>
    <t s="31">"And Yaakov settled," that Yaakov sought to settle in tranquility,</t>
    <t s="32">for the true meaning of settlement</t>
    <t s="33">("and he settled")</t>
    <t s="34">is to settle in tranquility],</t>
    <t s="35">unlike standing which indicates self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="36">And through the self-nullification of prayer,</t>
    <t s="37">the study of Torah after prayer is also with self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="38">and the revelation of Ein Sof is drawn into it.</t>
    <t s="39">And it can be said that this is the connection between the two interpretations in the Midrash</t>
    <t s="40">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="41">"And behold, a ladder was set upon the earth and its head reached the heavens,"</t>
    <t s="42">one interpretation: the ladder is the ramp</t>
    <t s="43">(prayer)</t>
    <t s="44">and the second interpretation: the ladder is Sinai</t>
    <t s="45">(Torah),</t>
    <t s="46">for through the preparation of the service of prayer, an elevation is made</t>
    <t s="47">(also)</t>
    <t s="48">in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="49">that the revelation of Ein Sof is drawn into it.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
